title: Remote Magnetic Actuation of Micrometric Probes for in situ 3D Mapping of Bacterial Biofilm Physical Properties
protocol: Pick a freshly grown colony from an LB agar plate.
Inoculate the colony into 5 ml liquid LB medium containing ampicillin and tetracycline.
Incubate for 5 to 6 hours at 37 °C on a shaking platform.
Add 100 µl of the bacterial culture to 5 ml minimum medium (M63B1) with 0.4% glucose and antibiotics.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C on a shaking platform.
After 16 hours, add 100 μl of the overnight culture to 5 ml M63B1 with 0.4% glucose.
Keep the tube at 37 °C on a shaking platform until an OD of 0.5 is reached.
Take 10 μl magnetic particles from the stock.
Wash them 3 times in 190 μl minimum medium using a magnetic sample rack.
Adjust particle concentration to 5 x 10^6 beads/ml.
Typically, mix 50 μl of washed bead solution with 950 µl M63B1 with 0.4% glucose.
Cut two square borosilicate glass capillaries (800 µm side length) to obtain two pieces each 8 cm long.
Glue the two capillary pieces on two glass slides cut in half, 2 cm apart with a 1 cm overhang on either end using super-glue.
Autoclave the entire setup and necessary tubing.
Gather mounted channel and trap 1 under laminar flow hood.
Gather tubing and connectors under laminar flow hood.
Gather two bubble traps (pediatric filter and homemade bubble trap) under laminar flow hood.
Gather clamps under laminar flow hood.
Fill 30 ml syringes with M63B1 and 0.4% glucose under laminar flow hood.
Connect 50 ml M63B1 syringe to the setup using Luer Lock connectors.
Connect pediatric bubble filter to the setup.
Connect homemade bubble trap to the setup.
Connect capillary to the setup.
Connect tubing to waste bottle.
Turn on syringe pump at rate of about 10 ml/hr.
Eliminate all bubbles in circuit carefully.
Flow medium through system for 10-15 min.
Mix 1 ml bacteria suspension (OD 0.5) with 1 ml washed bead solution.
Attach clamps before and after capillaries without closing.
Switch flow off.
Introduce bacterial-bead mixture into capillary using 1 ml syringe, holding tube ends to prevent air entry.
Re-attach tubing.
Close clamps.
Repeat the same procedure for the second capillary.
Check all tubes for bubbles.
Transfer the apparatus to the microscope and allow it to stand for 15-20 min.
Install the capillary onto the microscope stage with the waste container at a slightly higher level.
Elevate the bubble trap before the capillary slightly higher than the capillary plane.
Adjust the flow rate on the syringe pump and start the flow.
Focus on the capillary bottom plane.
Start the time-lapse recording of sample images.
Screw the magnetic tweezers on manually controlled X-Y-Z micromanipulators.
Screw the micromanipulators on the microscope stage to adjust the position of the tweezers relatively to the capillary.
Connect the tweezers to the function generator via the power amplifier.
Generate a 40 sec period with 24 sec zero signal and 16 sec of 4 A direct current.
Send a trigger to the bright field light shutter after 20 sec for synchronization.
Use the xy movement control to align the edge of the left-hand magnetic pole and the left-hand edge of the capillary in the same observation field.
Set the origin of the analysis referential at the intersection of x- and y-axes defined by the edge of the capillary and the edge of the pole piece.
Adjust the vertical position of the capillary using the fine focus control knob.
Typically, the first examined plane is located between 4 to 7 µm above the capillary bottom.
Manually trigger the image acquisition sequence of Video 1.
Trigger the 40 sec sequence by switching on the current generator.
Move the capillary to the neighboring right field by translating the microscope stage 250 µm to the left.
Generate Video 2 of slice 2.
Repeat operations to obtain required videos, moving along the x-axis and changing planes as necessary.
Prepare a glycerol solution by mixing 39.8 g of glycerol with 190 µl of bi-distilled water.
Add 10 μl of magnetic particles at a concentration of 2 x 10^9 particles/ml to the glycerol solution.
Fill an experimental channel with the prepared glycerol mixture.
Place the filled experimental channel on the microscope stage as described for biofilm samples.
Install the magnetic tweezers as indicated in section 4.
Apply magnetic force as specified in section 5.4.
Make time-lapse images to extract single particle velocity and its position in the capillary.
Derive calibration file based on applied force using Stokes law, F = 6πRηv (where R is radius of the particle).
Use "particle tracker" software to obtain text files with particle positions for all image stacks acquired as indicated in section 5.
Calculate particle displacement as a function of time using the acquisition frequency.
Using the force calibration file, convert the displacement curves to compliance curves (total compliance of the material — J(t)— as a function of time).
Adjust the creep compliance curves to the general Burgers model for viscoelastic materials.
Derive the viscoelastic parameters, J0, J1, η0, η1 for each particle according to the Burgers' formula.
